title: Feeding Bacteria to House Flies for Microbe Fate and Gene Expression Analysis
author: Dana Nayduch

steps.title: Sanitize and store pupae
steps.instruction: Collect pupae, optionally surface‑sanitize for 2 min each with gentle swirling in 10 % bleach, sterile H₂O, 100 % ethanol, and sterile H₂O; then store pupae in a sterile container (e.g., petri dish secured with rubber band or tape) or individually in 15 mL conical tubes until eclosion. Hold at 28 °C (or at room temperature, which may delay eclosion by a few days). After eclosion, separate emerged flies from puparia to reduce trans‑stadial bacterial contamination.

substeps.instruction: Surface‑sanitize: 2 min in 10 % bleach → sterile H₂O → 100 % ethanol → sterile H₂O (optional).
Incubate at 28 °C or room temperature (slower development).
Separate flies from puparia after eclosion.

steps.title: Prepare sterile fly containers
steps.instruction: Choose small petri dishes, 50 mL beakers covered with foil, or small plastic containers with lids (make air holes with a pin). Autoclave or wash/sanitize the containers, then place a ~15 × 15 mm parafilm square at the bottom of each container to receive the food droplet.

substeps.instruction: Select container type and create air holes if needed.
Add a 15 × 15 mm parafilm square to the bottom.

steps.title: Add sterile meal and transfer flies
steps.instruction: Prepare a sterile 10 % fly‑food solution or 10 % sucrose. Pipette 5–10 µL onto the parafilm square in each container. Anesthetize flies with CO₂ or chill in a freezer (~3 min), then transfer each newly eclosed (2–3 day‑old) fly to a container using soft forceps and close the lid tightly. The fly will wake, ingest the droplet (flushing gut bacteria and providing sustenance).

substeps.instruction: Transfer one fly per container with forceps.
Seal container; allow fly to recover and eat.

steps.title: Fast flies and optional second meal
steps.instruction: Hold the flies at room temperature and fast for 12 h. Optionally, after the first fast, briefly anesthetize (CO₂ or chilling), add a second 5–10 µL sterile 10 % sucrose droplet, then fast a second 12 h before feeding bacteria.

substeps.instruction: If desired, anesthetize briefly and add a second 10 % sucrose droplet.
Fast another 12 h before bacterial feeding.

steps.title: Grow bacterial seed cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate a large volume (100–250 mL) of appropriate broth with a single colony of the target bacterium and grow overnight (8–12 h) at the temperature, RPM, and media specified in the bacterial protocol. Use a flask at least twice the culture volume (e.g., 250 mL flask for 100 mL culture, 500 mL flask for 250 mL). Do not exceed 8–12 h incubation to avoid bacterial death.

substeps.instruction: Pick a single colony into 100–250 mL broth.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial feeding culture
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the overnight seed culture to sterile broth (typically 100 mL total volume) and incubate at 37 °C while rotating at 200 RPM until the desired OD₆₀₀ is reached. Aim for an OD that yields ~10⁸ CFU/mL, which provides ≥2 × 10⁵ CFU in a 2 µL droplet (≥10⁵ CFU per fly for immune‑stimulation assays).

substeps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL seed to ~100 mL fresh broth.

steps.title: Feed bacteria to flies
steps.instruction: After the 12 h fast, place the flies in a 37 °C incubator for ~15 min, then return them to room temperature. Using a pipette, carefully dispense a 2 µL droplet of the bacterial culture onto the parafilm square in each container (anesthetize if necessary). Verify that the full 2 µL has been released.

substeps.instruction: Place 2 µL bacterial droplet on parafilm.

steps.title: Select flies that ingested bacteria
steps.instruction: Observe flies and mark containers whose flies ingest the entire 2 µL droplet within 30 min. Discard any flies that ingest partially, later than 30 min, or not at all. For BSL‑2 bacteria, keep infected flies in their primary containers and place those containers inside secondary containers (large bins, cages, etc.) that also allow adequate air circulation.

substeps.instruction: If BSL‑2, store primary containers inside secondary, ventilated containers.

steps.title: Enumerate fed bacteria via plating
steps.instruction: Serially dilute the stock culture (the same culture used for the fed aliquot) in sterile media or PBS: e.g., add 100 µL stock to 900 µL diluent for each 10‑fold step. Plate appropriate dilutions on selective agar containing the relevant antibiotics. Incubate plates at 37 °C for 24 h, then count colonies under a UV lightbox, counting only GFP‑expressing colonies.
